name: App Management Console — approval frames
description: Contract-freeze UX artifacts for the App Management Console (FF-EPIC-20) — the management surface FuzeFront has never had. Three flows: (1) list every registered app (searchable/filterable/paginated) with lifecycle state, visibility and owning org; (2) open one app to view/edit its settings & attributes and run its lifecycle (activate/suspend), built-ins non-deletable; (3) manage where an app is installed and at what scope (org/portal/user). Distinct from federated-apps (the register→activate add-app flow). Approving a flow approves its visual + interaction model AND its component/package/contract build inventory before any UI is written. Flows 1 & 2 bind to the REAL @fuzefront/app-registry-client; flow 3 (installations/scopes) is anticipated and commissioned by these frames. frontend-test-engineer drives Playwright against these via the data-frame / data-* hooks.

real.usedFor: List all apps; read/edit one app's manifest (display, visibility, routing/entry, config attributes); delete (non-builtin); lifecycle transitions activate/suspend; health via heartbeat. Base path /api/v1/app-registry.

anticipated.openapi: app installations/scopes surface (NOT frozen — commissioned by these frames, modelled on the portal precedent's portal_apps)
anticipated.usedFor: View/add/remove where an app is installed and at what scope level (organization/portal/user). Every reference carries its type (targetType), never a bare id (identifier-standard). Targets authorized via Permit.

contract.openapi: app installations/scopes surface (NOT frozen — commissioned by these frames)

dsPrimitivesNeeded: Tabs — app-detail tab strip; not in @fuzefront/design-system today
StatusPill — semantic lifecycle / visibility / installation state pill

commissionedByApproval: App installations/scopes surface (GET/POST/DELETE /apps/{slug}/installations) — does not exist in the app-registry contract today; commissioned by these frames, modelled on the portal precedent's portal_apps.
409 CONFLICT on concurrent manifest edit (PUT /apps/{slug}) — proposed optimistic-concurrency guard rendered inline (frame f, f6).
422 VALIDATION on an invalid manifest field (e.g. entry URL) rendered inline on the field, never a toast (frame f, f6).
403 FORBIDDEN_TARGET on adding an installation to a target outside the caller's authority (frame g, g7); read-only fail-closed surfaces on missing apps:write / apps:activate (frames e5, f1, g4).

frames.label: (a) All applications
frames.summary: Searchable, filterable, paginated table (with grid toggle) of every registered app: icon+name, slug, lifecycle state (registered/activated/suspended), visibility (private/organization/public/marketplace), owning org, integration. Row → detail. Built-ins tagged.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Rows render from GET /api/v1/app-registry/apps (cursor-paginated — data-action='load-more' fetches the next page, never an unbounded fetch). Search filters by name/slug; filter chips narrow by status, visibility and owning org, applied server-side as query params and reflected in the URL. State pill maps status: registered=warning, activated=success, suspended=error. A row is a link to /apps/{slug}. builtin apps are tagged (data-builtin='true'). Loading/empty/no-results/error/read-only are contract — see frame (e).

frames.label: (b) App detail
frames.summary: One app at a glance: header (icon/name/state/visibility), lifecycle actions (Suspend when activated / Activate when suspended), and an overview definition list (display name, immutable slug, owning org, integration, entry/route, menu chrome, health, installation count). Tabs into settings and installations.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Header + overview bind to GET /api/v1/app-registry/apps/{slug} (AppManifest). Lifecycle is state-driven and mutually exclusive: an activated app shows Suspend (POST /apps/{slug}/suspend), a registered/suspended app shows Activate (POST /apps/{slug}/activate) — never both; requires apps:activate. A caller without the scope sees no lifecycle control (fail-closed, frame f). builtin apps hide Delete entirely. Health derives from GET /apps/{slug}/heartbeat.

frames.label: (c) Settings & attributes
frames.summary: Settings/attributes editor: display name, icon uploader, visibility select, entry/remote URL, route/mount path, and configuration attributes as key/value rows (add/remove). Slug rendered read-only (immutable). Sticky save bar with dirty indicator.
frames.acceptanceNotes: Save is PUT /api/v1/app-registry/apps/{slug} replacing the AppManifest; requires apps:write. Slug and builtin are immutable — rendered read-only, and a changed slug is rejected server-side. Visibility options are the contract enum (private/organization/public/marketplace). Attributes edit manifest config keys (menuLabel, chrome.menu, mode, …). A 422 renders inline on the offending field; a 409 concurrent-edit and a 403 denial are contract (frame f). A caller without apps:write sees the whole form read-only with no Save affordance.

frames.label: (d) Installations & scopes
frames.summary: Table of where the app is installed: target (org/portal/user), scope level, installed-by, status. Add-installation dialog (scope level + target picker) and per-row remove. An installation whose target was removed/suspended shows an orphaned status.
frames.acceptanceNotes: ANTICIPATED surface. Rows from GET /api/v1/app-registry/apps/{slug}/installations. Add is POST …/installations { scopeLevel, targetId, targetType } — every reference carries its type (organization/portal/user), never a bare id. Remove is DELETE …/installations/{id} behind a confirm. Only targets the caller administers are selectable; a cross-tenant target is 403 (frame g, g7). An installation whose target portal was removed/suspended renders data-installation-status='orphaned' and stays removable — it never crashes the table (frame g, g5).

frames.label: (e) App-list states
frames.summary: The app list's contract states: loading skeleton, empty registry, no-results (search/filter matched nothing), load error+retry, and the fail-closed read-only/permission-denied list with every management affordance absent.
frames.acceptanceNotes: e1 loading = aria-busy skeleton for GET /apps. e2 empty is a truly empty registry (distinct copy + register CTA). e3 no-results is a non-empty registry with a search/filter that matched nothing (distinct state + clear-filters). e4 error shows data-action='retry'. e5 is the rule: a 403 renders the list READ-ONLY (no create/edit/suspend/install controls rendered — not disabled-on-click), shown in place, NEVER a sign-in redirect (only 401 re-authenticates).

frames.label: (f) Detail & editor states
frames.summary: Detail/editor contract states: read-only (fail-closed) detail, suspended app with limited actions (Activate not Suspend), built-in immutable (Delete disabled), app with no editable settings (disabled Save, not a broken form), suspend confirm, and save failures (422 inline / 409 preserves form / 403 in place).
frames.acceptanceNotes: f1 read-only is fail-closed: no management affordance rendered on a 403, never shown-then-403'd. f2 a suspended app offers Activate (not Suspend) and pauses installation targeting. f3 builtin=true disables Delete client-side and the API refuses it (BUILTIN_IMMUTABLE). f4 an app with no editable settings shows a disabled Save with an explanatory empty state, not an empty broken form. f5 suspend is POST /apps/{slug}/suspend behind a confirm. f6: 422 VALIDATION renders inline on the field, 409 CONFLICT preserves the form, 403 FORBIDDEN is shown in place.

frames.label: (g) Installation states
frames.summary: The installations surface's contract states: loading, no installations, load error, read-only (fail-closed), orphaned target (removed/suspended portal → status, not crash), remove confirm, and cross-tenant add denied (403).
frames.acceptanceNotes: g1 loading skeleton for GET …/installations. g2 empty is an app installed nowhere. g3 non-2xx with retry. g4 read-only fail-closed: no Add/Remove rendered. g5 is the epic's edge case: an installation whose target portal was removed/suspended renders data-installation-status='orphaned' from its own record and stays removable — it must NOT crash or blank the list. g6 remove is DELETE …/installations/{id} behind a confirm. g7 add authorizes the target via Permit; a target outside the caller's authority is 403 FORBIDDEN_TARGET, shown in place.
